ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Ophthalmology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Red, swollen eyes with watery discharge for two days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The neonate presents to ophthalmology clinic following ED visits for gastroschisis, cyanosis, and hemorrhagic disease, and is status post arterial switch and gastroschisis repair with perinatal HIV exposure and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis. He is brought to pediatric clinic by his mother, who reports that her son has had red, swollen eyes with a watery discharge for the past two days. The mother denies fever or irritability in the infant. She mentions the delivery was vaginal and she had a history of sexually transmitted infections but was not sure which ones.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Gastroschisis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Transposition of the great arteries (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Neonatal sepsis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vitamin K deficiency (Hemorrhagic disease of the newborn) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Status post surgical repair of gastroschisis with anticipated short bowel syndrome
- Status post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries
- Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
- History of perinatal HIV exposure
- History of hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (late vitamin K deficiency bleeding)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary closure of gastroschisis with silo placement
- Arterial switch operation
- Microlaryngoscopy and bronchoscopy with papilloma debridement

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Zidovudine 2 mg/kg orally every 6 hours (neonatal HIV prophylaxis)
- Vitamin D supplementation 400 IU orally daily
- Iron supplementation 2 mg/kg orally daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal HIV infection (diagnosed, adherent to antiretroviral therapy)
- Maternal human papillomavirus infection (source of neonatal laryngeal papillomatosis)
- Maternal history of chlamydia trachomatis infection
- Home birth attended by unlicensed birth attendant
- Unremarkable paternal medical history

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

VITAL SIGNS:
The infant's vital signs are within normal limits.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant appears well, with bilateral mild eyelid swelling and chemosis. There is a mucopurulent discharge from both eyes. The corneas are clear, and the remainder of the eye examination is unremarkable.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. James O'Brien, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Persistent bleeding from umbilical stump

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient, status post repair of gastroschisis and arterial switch for d-transposition of the great arteries with perinatal HIV and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis, presented earlier today for sepsis evaluation. He returns with bleeding. He was delivered at home by an unlicensed birth attendant and had not yet been seen by professionals before presentation. The delivery was uneventful, and the infant has been feeding well at home. However, the parents grew concerned when they noticed that his diaper was repeatedly stained with blood near the umbilicus, and the bleeding had not stopped despite attempted pressure. He has no bruising elsewhere.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Gastroschisis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Transposition of the great arteries (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Neonatal sepsis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Status post surgical repair of gastroschisis with anticipated short bowel syndrome
- Status post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries
- Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
- History of perinatal HIV exposure
- History of hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (late vitamin K deficiency bleeding)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary closure of gastroschisis with silo placement
- Arterial switch operation
- Microlaryngoscopy and bronchoscopy with papilloma debridement

MEDICATIONS:
The infant has not received any vaccinations or medications since birth.

Home Medications:
- Zidovudine 2 mg/kg orally every 6 hours (neonatal HIV prophylaxis)
- Vitamin D supplementation 400 IU orally daily
- Iron supplementation 2 mg/kg orally daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
No family history of bleeding disorders

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, he is alert and active with normal vital signs. There is mild oozing of blood from the base of the umbilical stump, but no petechiae, purpura, or mucosal bleeding. There is no hepatosplenomegaly. His anterior fontanelle is flat, and the rest of the exam is unremarkable.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive cyanosis at 12 hours of age

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Following his earlier presentation on the date of birth for visible abdominal wall defect, the 12-hour-old male neonate is brought to the emergency department by his concerned parents due to progressive cyanosis. The pregnancy was uneventful, and the mother had regular prenatal care. The baby was born at term via spontaneous vaginal delivery. The mother reports that the baby appeared pink at birth but has become increasingly blue, especially during feeding.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Gastroschisis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Status post surgical repair of gastroschisis with anticipated short bowel syndrome
- Status post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries
- Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
- History of perinatal HIV exposure
- History of hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (late vitamin K deficiency bleeding)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Primary closure of gastroschisis with silo placement
- Arterial switch operation
- Microlaryngoscopy and bronchoscopy with papilloma debridement

MEDICATIONS:

- Zidovudine 2 mg/kg orally every 6 hours (neonatal HIV prophylaxis)
- Vitamin D supplementation 400 IU orally daily
- Iron supplementation 2 mg/kg orally daily

ALLERGIES:

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal HIV infection (diagnosed, adherent to antiretroviral therapy)
- Maternal human papillomavirus infection (source of neonatal laryngeal papillomatosis)
- Maternal history of chlamydia trachomatis infection
- Home birth attended by unlicensed birth attendant
- Unremarkable paternal medical history

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (infant).

VITAL SIGNS:
The pulse oximetry shows an oxygen saturation of 85% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the neonate is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 70 breaths per minute and has central cyanosis. Auscultation of the heart reveals a single loud second heart sound (S2) and no murmurs. The extremities are cool to touch, and the pulses are diminished.

LABORATORY DATA:
An arterial blood gas reveals:
- pH: 7.35
- PaCO2: 40 mmHg
- PaO2: 50 mmHg
- HCO3-: 22 mEq/L

IMAGING:
A chest X-ray shows a narrow mediastinum and an "egg on a string" appearance.
